rv.q: Henner’s pitch-perfect performance captures the unflappable narcissism of an entire generation.

Although The Ask poses interesting questions about generational political differences and wealth, framing them through a two-person showdown, the play never amps up the stakes enough to go all in on the drama.
Once the central conflict finally emerges, the production becomes considerably more compelling.
Two fine actresses have been trapped in a dull, existential absurdity.

cn.t: Critics find this ACLU fundraising drama ideologically driven but dramatically inert, with most citing a lack of tension and build despite its timely premise about generational divides over money and politics.
